races.name: Betfred 'Bet Builder' Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Oj Lifestyle
runners_data.note: Has won twice at this course-and-distance on Good, the most convincing going match in the field; hold-up style suits a strongly-run race better than today's expected measured tempo, but his Epsom record is a genuine asset if a gap appears.
runners_data.comment: Hit the line well to land a handicap at Brighton by a length ten days ago, Oj Lifestyle arrives in sharp form and goes well at this track. Suited to this trip and ground, the addition of tongue-tie and cheekpieces adds interest and the yard is in good order.

runners_data.name: Imperial Cult
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner, back-to-back winner heading in, with a clean jumping gate and every tactical advantage; his two recent wins came on Standard rather than Good, which is a mild query, but unchallenged control outweighs that concern.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back handicap wins show Imperial Cult in fine fettle, and he landed his most recent at Kempton by three lengths displaying a willing attitude. Effective over a range of distances, he will want a positive ride here as this trip is towards the shorter end of his range.

runners_data.name: Bobacious
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who has shown Good-ground form at 10f, but a run of disappointing efforts on Standard and soft surfaces clouds confidence; trainer has just one runner in the 14-day window and no obvious angle to exploit here.
runners_data.comment: Suited to this distance and surface, Bobacious was successful at Epsom last year over this course and distance and enjoys forcing the pace. His recent efforts have been modest — winless in his last five — and he was a shade below his best when fourth at Lingfield latest.

runners_data.name: Hello Cotai
runners_data.note: Showed a sharp 10f win on Good last time under Jim Boyle's patient hold-up approach, and the trainer saddles two runners today; the 30-day break is manageable given that form read and this going suits, though he needs the race to be run faster than Imperial Cult will likely set it.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap at Windsor last time out by a length off a reduced mark, Hello Cotai appears to have returned to his best form and remains competitively positioned. He handles any going and is suited to this trip, making him a solid danger.

runners_data.name: Super Hit
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing sort fitted with hood/tongue-tie who has mixed form at 7-8f and steps up slightly in trip today; the James Owen stable is in strong form (10/54 over 14 days) and a patient hold-up-to-prominent switch here could give him a tactical advantage.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in his last six starts, Super Hit tracked the pace when fourth at Redcar last time, performing at his level over a distance that suits, though beaten by a wide margin. First-time hood and tongue-tie are a new angle, and conditions here are fine.

runners_data.name: Mrembo
runners_data.note: Strong recent form in 12f handicaps on Good — four placings and a win in that exact scenario — but naturally wants to race off the pace; shown in midfield here because the rear is overcrowded, meaning she is unlikely to find her ideal position and the style-fit discount applies.
runners_data.comment: In fair recent trim, Mrembo ran her race last time when fourth beaten only 1½l off this same mark, and she returns to identical conditions. Effective over this distance and at her best on a sound surface, the fitting of first-time cheekpieces adds an angle.

runners_data.name: Beta Reader
runners_data.note: Has placed twice on Good ground at 10f and ran creditably from off the pace, but a 55-day absence is the longest break in the field; similarly displaced from her natural hold-up spot by the congested rear, so cannot be expected to reproduce her best without recapturing that position.
runners_data.comment: Showed a tendency to pull hard but kept on for third at Windsor on his most recent outing, 55 days ago, and there is scope to build on that with first-time cheekpieces fitted. He handles this trip and ground, though the lengthy absence means he will need to show his peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Haveagobeau
runners_data.note: Prominent-to-prominent type who has been placed in three of five runs at this trip, and Good-ground form reads positively; represents Jim Boyle alongside Hello Cotai, and sitting just off Imperial Cult from a handy pitch is exactly the role this horse is built for.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Lingfield last time out, ten lengths adrift of the winner, Haveagobeau needs a meaningful improvement to figure here. He does handle this trip and probably acts on most surfaces, but he is the lowest-rated runner on our figures and requires a significant step forward.

runners_data.name: Turpin
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse pushed into midfield by redistribution and tagged with a fade-in-finish flag — two significant strikes against him; very limited upside in a race where the pace is expected to be unhurried and the rear of the field is where any pace would need to be to generate late momentum.
runners_data.comment: Performed to his level at Brighton last time when fifth, beaten 4½l, and this trip and ground suit him well enough. Yet to score in recent starts, he is capable of keeping on for minor honours if conditions fall right but faces a competitive field.

races.paceDynamic: Imperial Cult is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him early, he will stride off at his own rhythm from the gates and control the tempo through Epsom's undulating 1m2f. The pace he sets is likely to be sustainable rather than brutal, giving him every chance to preserve energy for the home straight where Epsom's camber and finish reward horses with residual stamina. This shape — a single unchallenged leader dictating a measured gallop — classically favours prominent-to-lead types and horses that can sit just off the pace and pounce, rather than deep closers who need a truly hot pace to produce their best. Mrembo, Beta Reader, and Turpin are genuine hold-up horses but have been mapped into midfield because the rear is over-subscribed; they are unlikely to reproduce their natural trailing positions, and their chances in a shape that requires late ground-making must be discounted accordingly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Imperial Cult Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Imperial Cult settles cleanly in front, controls a measured gallop, and the field fails to mount a sustained challenge until the home straight.
scenarios.body: If Imperial Cult settles cleanly in front, controls a measured gallop, and the field fails to mount a sustained challenge until the home straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Super Hit or Haveagobeau tracks Imperial Cult closely enough to challenge from 2f out as the pace steadies and they grind past a tiring leader.
scenarios.body: If Super Hit or Haveagobeau tracks Imperial Cult closely enough to challenge from 2f out as the pace steadies and they grind past a tiring leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and a hold-up horse can find a clear run up the Epsom straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and a hold-up horse can find a clear run up the Epsom straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the mapped-midfield horses — Mrembo, Beta Reader, or Turpin — manage to secure a position closer to their preferred hold-up ground and the race develops unusually fast.
scenarios.body: If the mapped-midfield horses — Mrembo, Beta Reader, or Turpin — manage to secure a position closer to their preferred hold-up ground and the race develops unusually fast.

watchPoints.text: Imperial Cult's early jumping and settling behaviour is the single biggest race-shaping factor — if he dwells or is slow into stride, the entire dynamic shifts and a mid-pack challenge becomes far more plausible.

Haveagobeau and Super Hit are likely to contest the same prominent berth just off the leader; if both push forward simultaneously they could inadvertently inject more pace than the map predicts and compromise their own stamina.
Mrembo, Beta Reader, and Turpin are all natural hold-up horses squeezed into midfield — watch for traffic congestion around the 6f mark when Epsom's descent begins and the field tightens sharply.

Hello Cotai won last time on Good at 10f and is equipped to race closer than her hold-up tag implies if the pace is gentle — watch whether Luke Catton elects to push forward early and alter the expected race shape.

Oj Lifestyle's rider Toby Moore claims 7lb and the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 4/20 is the strongest in the field; if the pace does strengthen in the latter stages, this horse's Epsom course record makes him a shape-beneficiary worth monitoring.

races.name: Betfred Play Fred's 5 Million EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Confernation
runners_data.comment: Ran to a consistent level on his second start when fourth at Leicester, beaten 2¼l, Confernation has solid claims over this trip and surface. He is yet to score but has run with credit in both starts and rates an honest mid-range contender.

runners_data.name: Foscarini
runners_data.comment: Showed ability on debut despite being beaten six lengths when fifth on soft ground, and this switch to 7f on a sounder surface looks a considerably more favourable test. He is our top-rated runner and the one to beat on these figures.

runners_data.name: Printing Money
runners_data.comment: Matched his debut level on his most recent outing when sixth at Ripon, beaten eight lengths, and goes from the widest draw in the field. The pedigree carries pace and he may develop into a more interesting proposition once eligible for handicaps, but he is the lowest on our figures and needs to do considerably better here.

runners_data.name: Shemiyla Star
runners_data.comment: Ran an eye-catching race on his only start, going down by a neck in a maiden at Pontefract and showing himself clearly effective at 6f. A step up to 7f should unlock further improvement, and he has the profile to make an impact, though he has only the one run to his name.

runners_data.name: Bullrider
runners_data.comment: A 30,000 euro breeze-up purchase by Blackbeard, Bullrider is unraced but makes his debut for a yard with a strong record with youngsters and has the profile to make an immediate mark. The dam is unraced though related to useful performers; he is worth treating with respect.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Galore
runners_data.comment: A 35,000gns Sergei Prokofiev colt making his debut, Whiskey Galore has a dam effective at 7f which suits the trip. The trainer's yard has been quiet of late, though, and he may need this first outing to show his best.

runners_data.name: Wise And Wonderful
runners_data.comment: Stepped up on her debut effort when runner-up at Wetherby latest, beaten 3¼l over 7f, and this filly is trained by a handler with a strong record at this course. She handles 6-7f on a sound surface and has good claims if she continues that progress; yet to score.

runners_data.name: Mojito Madness
runners_data.comment: Showed greenness on his debut at Leicester, pulling hard but clearly possessing ability before being beaten eight lengths. The trainer is doing well and there is scope for considerable improvement as he learns to settle; he handles this trip and surface.

races.name: Betfred 'Nifty 50' Handicap

runners_data.name: Desert Cop
runners_data.note: Won over C&D on Good ground and has placed at Epsom multiple times — strong course form is the key angle here; races as a genuine hold-up type from the rear and needs the pace to be honest enough to make ground, which is not guaranteed with a single front-runner dictating.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a Windsor handicap by 1½ lengths last time and meets this field under a penalty with first-time cheekpieces; he handles this trip on a sound surface and the yard has a strong record in this contest, though he draws from the widest stall.

runners_data.name: Dream Composer
runners_data.note: Trainer Tony Carroll in strong current form (10/51 T14) and won last time out at 5f on Good, but six furlongs is a step up in trip and the horse's five-furlong focus is a mild concern; hold-up style means it requires a true pace and the 9-day turnaround looks fine.|
runners_data.comment: Sealed a narrow Windsor handicap success last time, finishing powerfully to take it by a nose at his best over 5f; first-time cheekpieces are added but the step up in distance and extra weight make this a harder test.

runners_data.name: Amazing Journey
runners_data.note: The race's confirmed pace-setter and likely to bowl along uncontested — strong tactical position, though the 21-day break and a step back to 6f after two runs at 7f are worth noting; a 3yo allowed to control a modest gallop in a handicap is not to be dismissed, even if the style tag suggests a degree of positional compromise.|
runners_data.comment: Showed his best form to take a Kempton handicap by 2½ lengths three weeks ago, looking well within himself over this trip and ground; he is now 6lb higher but retains the potential to improve further and heads our rankings.

runners_data.name: Independent Expert
runners_data.note: Sound form over this trip on Good ground is present but rare in this horse's record — naturally a hold-up type who has been running over 7f and 8f, and the drop to 6f at Epsom against faster types asks questions; T14 blank (0/7) for Best and 36 days off add further caution.|
runners_data.comment: Arrives from Irish racing with questions to answer at this level; she was beaten 6 lengths in a claimer on her most recent outing and, on our figures, sits at the foot of this field with plenty to prove at the current mark.

runners_data.name: Havana Rum
runners_data.note: Ethan Tindall claims 5lb and has placed at prominent positions in this trip range before — Fahey yard in fair current trim (5/56 T14) and the horse's prominent style should allow it to sit in a nice stalking spot if Amazing Journey leads cleanly; best form came on softer ground, so Good is a mild query.|
runners_data.comment: Produced his strongest finish in the closing stages at Chester last time, coming on after a tardy beginning to be beaten 3 lengths off a 1lb higher mark; he is without a win in recent starts and his rating is easing, though the trip and ground suit him.

runners_data.name: Sir Garfield
runners_data.note: Won last time over 6f on Good ground and represents the yard's best recent form angle — naturally wants to race prominently but with several others eyeing the same ground, it is pushed into a midfield mapping and may not get its preferred berth; 84-day absence is the sharpest concern.|
runners_data.comment: Returned from a break to take a Catterick handicap by ¾ of a length on his most recent outing, showing he retains his ability over this trip; first-time blinkers are added, though his absence of 84 days makes the degree of residual fitness uncertain.

runners_data.name: Goldwork
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton yard in modest current form but this horse has placed twice at 6f on Good ground and the prominent style suits the expected race shape well; a 3yo on just 130lbs with recent experience at this trip is worth respecting even if finishing positions have been inconsistent.|
runners_data.comment: Matched expectations at Newmarket last time, beaten 2 lengths at this mark over 6f on good ground; he is our second-ranked runner and fits this trip and conditions well, with first-time cheekpieces to aid focus, though he is yet to win in recent outings.

runners_data.name: Mumayaz
runners_data.note: Consistent record at 6f on Good at face value — won at the trip and running style naturally favours a forward position, but with the field stacked with similar types, its berth may be compromised and the 7lb claim rider (Myla Coppins) adds uncertainty; ran just 2 days ago, which is the freshness flag to monitor.|
runners_data.comment: Finished third and beaten 4 lengths off a mark 1lb higher than today's last time, running to his level; he handles varied going and is arguably still fairly treated, though he comes off a quick turnaround and sits in the bottom half of our rankings.

races.paceDynamic: Amazing Journey is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should be able to dictate a measured, controlled tempo from the front on Good ground at Epsom. That sustainable pace — set by a single, unchallenged horse — means the race is unlikely to be run at a scorching early gallop, and the first two furlongs should not be punishingly fast. This shape classically rewards those racing prominently just behind the leader, able to pounce off a steady early clip, rather than closers who need a true test to make up ground late. The field carries more prominent and press-from-front types than the shape can accommodate: Sir Garfield, Mumayaz, and Havana Rum are all genuine forwardly-placed horses, but with Amazing Journey controlling matters, at least one or two of those will be unable to hold their natural position and will end up shuffled wider or further back — with Havana Rum and Goldwork, having cleaner prominent claims in this specific shape, most likely to actually secure the ground just off the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Rails Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Amazing Journey dictates an uncontested, moderate tempo and those tracking her closely get a ground-saving run.
scenarios.body: If Amazing Journey dictates an uncontested, moderate tempo and those tracking her closely get a ground-saving run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Amazing Journey is genuinely moderate and she gets away clean with a field that fails to close.
scenarios.body: If the pace set by Amazing Journey is genuinely moderate and she gets away clean with a field that fails to close.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Fly Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively strong early and the field strings out, giving hold-up horses a meaningful gap to close.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves deceptively strong early and the field strings out, giving hold-up horses a meaningful gap to close.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types clash for position early and the race becomes a messy, high-tempo scramble that suits none of them.
scenarios.body: If multiple prominent types clash for position early and the race becomes a messy, high-tempo scramble that suits none of them.

watchPoints.text: Amazing Journey's early sectionals — if she is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a genuine clip she could steal a winning lead, but any crowding from Sir Garfield or Mumayaz in the opening furlong could unsettle her and fundamentally reshape the pace picture.

Sir Garfield and Mumayaz both want the same forward ground — watch the first furlong for a positional squeeze between them that could force one or both wider and further back than ideal, wasting energy at a track where position early on the straight six matters.

Mumayaz ran only two days ago — monitor paddock demeanour and early running for any signs of residual fatigue, as a horse stepping back out so quickly could either be in flying form or under-recovered.

Desert Cop's pace dependency is real — if Amazing Journey controls an honest but not extreme tempo, the ground may not open up quickly enough for a horse coming from last place over a straight Epsom six, so watch how the early splits look.|

Independent Expert's redistribution from hold-up to a midfield mapping understates how far back it may actually race — if it ends up last or second-last as its natural style dictates, the six-furlong Epsom straight may not be long enough to reel in a controlled leader.|

races.name: Betfred 'The Classic Bookmaker' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Analogical
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's patient placing record is a major angle here — this horse has won at 1m4f on Good and ran third at the same trip and going, giving him strong course-profile credentials; his prominent style should see him comfortably fill a front-rank berth behind Alma Latina, which suits.
runners_data.comment: Pulled hard and fell short of his best last time, finishing 5 lengths adrift off this mark; he tends to lead and the first-time cheekpieces may assist, but he needs to find considerably more and is ranked ninth on our figures.

runners_data.name: Mr Freedom
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with multiple places at 1m4f on Good ground, most recently third at this trip in this company; prominent racer who should get a clean run tracking the leader, though a soft-ground mark and older age are mild concerns.
runners_data.comment: Failed to see out the trip on soft ground at his last start, held in a handicap despite solid prior form; the move to a sounder surface today is an obvious plus and first-time cheekpieces are fitted, making it fair to expect a better showing.

runners_data.name: Arcturus Flame
runners_data.note: Placed in three consecutive runs including twice at 1m4f on Good, but his natural front-running instinct will be frustrated here — there are simply too many prominent horses in this field for him to get the position he needs, and he is likely to end up racing out of his comfort zone in midfield.
runners_data.comment: Finished second at Salisbury on his most recent start, beaten 4½ lengths while running to his level; he handles a range of trips and ground and is in decent form, with first-time blinkers now added, but he is yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Sir William
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's hold-up performer has a win and a second at 1m2f on Good but steps up to 1m4f; Saffie Osborne takes the mount and the extra distance should theoretically suit, though the OR=75 mark and 32-day absence require monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Ran well short of his best at Beverley last time, held in a handicap despite trying cheekpieces; he stays this trip and handles the ground, but is yet to score in recent starts and needs a significant improvement on that latest effort.

runners_data.name: Double Red
runners_data.note: Won twice at 1m on Soft and placed at 1m2f on Good, but this 1m4f trip on quicker ground is an unknown; a genuine prominent type, he is pushed back in the pace map and will likely face traffic, which markedly reduces his effectiveness in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Found the tempo beyond him when fourth and beaten 12 lengths last time, but steps up to 12f for the first time today and that extra distance could well play to his strengths; effective on a sound surface, he is 1lb lower and ranks second on our figures.

runners_data.name: Central Command
runners_data.note: Three wins from his last four starts including twice on Standard and once on Good at 1m2f; the Crisford stable is firing at 5/28 over 14 days and the step to 1m4f on Good looks well within compass for this three-year-old with a rising profile.
runners_data.comment: Dug deep to take a Doncaster handicap by a head last time, continuing a progressive sequence; he has experience at this trip and excels on a sound surface, though he wears a visor for the first time and faces a 5lb penalty today.

runners_data.name: Alma Latina
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly has only three runs but all three have been on Good at 1m2f, winning the latest; she steps up to 1m4f here as confirmed front-runner, and while her hold on the lead looks secure, the extra two furlongs and a first handicap start represent genuine unknowns.
runners_data.comment: Got off the mark at Pontefract last time, taking a maiden by 3½ lengths with a performance that suggests there is more to come; the step up to 12f looks well suited to her and, backed by a strong yard, she heads our rankings here.

runners_data.name: Timber Twelve
runners_data.note: Won twice over 1m on Standard and ran fourth at 1m2f on Good; Michael Bell's three-year-old steps into 1m4f handicap company on turf for the first time, and while the prominent style suits the race shape, his limited sim-going record (0 wins on turf) is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Ran below expectations at Chester last time, held by 5 lengths over a shorter trip; this is a significant step up in distance and his stamina over 12f is unproven, while the yard's current form is a further point to weigh, though the conditions may suit.

runners_data.name: Electrical
runners_data.note: Brian Toomey's three-year-old won over 6f on Good but has posted 7th and 6th in his most recent two turf starts; this is a steep rise in trip and the hold-up style only works if the pace is truly honest — a speculative entry at best.
runners_data.comment: Held well on soft ground at Chepstow last time, failing to show his best; he is unproven at this distance but is a sibling of a 14f winner, which makes the step up in trip interesting — the return to better ground is also a factor in his favour.

runners_data.name: Tabasko
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old has placed at 1m on Soft and Standard but his true hold-up style gets redistributed to midfield here, where he ends up neither holding-up nor prominent; 39 days off and no wins on Good ground make this a tough ask in his current profile.
runners_data.comment: Kept her form at Salisbury last time, beaten 5 lengths in a handicap; this step up to 12f is worth considering given she may stay the trip in time, but she sits at the foot of our rankings and is yet to score in recent starts.

races.paceDynamic: Alma Latina is the confirmed front-runner and, with no other natural leader to press her, she should dictate from the outset at a sustainable gallop around Epsom's unique contours. The field does, however, carry genuine pace congestion: Arcturus Flame, Double Red, Analogical, Mr Freedom and Timber Twelve are all prominent types who cannot all slot into their preferred position, meaning the early exchanges behind Alma Latina will involve some positional jostling that could compress the pace rather than stretch it. With Alma Latina able to control tempo without serious pressure, she sets a rhythm that rewards horses travelling smoothly in behind rather than those forced wide or into a scrimmage early. This race shape most strongly favours confirmed hold-up runners — Central Command, Sir William and Electrical — who can track the controlled pace through Tattenham Corner and deploy their finishing kicks down the straight, provided the gallop is honest enough to see them home; the uncontested front-runner scenario also gives Alma Latina a live chance to simply steal the race if the chasing pack spend too long sorting themselves out. The field holds more prominent types than the pace map can accommodate, with Analogical and Mr Freedom most likely to actually secure the positions directly behind Alma Latina given their class and recency advantage over Arcturus Flame and Double Red, who are likely shuffled wider or further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alma Latina Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Alma Latina gets a clear lead at a measured tempo and no prominent rival has the foot to close the gap until Tattenham Corner.
scenarios.body: If Alma Latina gets a clear lead at a measured tempo and no prominent rival has the foot to close the gap until Tattenham Corner.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the controlled front-running pace is honest enough to string the field out and leave genuine closers with momentum down the Epsom straight.
scenarios.body: If the controlled front-running pace is honest enough to string the field out and leave genuine closers with momentum down the Epsom straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If positional chaos behind Alma Latina resolves early, allowing Analogical or Mr Freedom to track her smoothly and ambush her near home.
scenarios.body: If positional chaos behind Alma Latina resolves early, allowing Analogical or Mr Freedom to track her smoothly and ambush her near home.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes, Backmarkers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If early positional scrapping elevates the tempo materially and Alma Latina is pressed into going faster than intended, collapsing the field for true closers.
scenarios.body: If early positional scrapping elevates the tempo materially and Alma Latina is pressed into going faster than intended, collapsing the field for true closers.

watchPoints.text: Alma Latina sets the pace completely unchallenged — watch whether Hector Crouch elects to dawdle or builds a genuine lead from the off, as any tactical error at the front dictates the outcome for the entire field.

Central Command's recent three-win sequence and the Crisford stable's 14-day strike rate of 5/28 mark him as the most dangerous closer in the field — watch how Daniel Muscutt positions him through Tattenham Corner.

Arcturus Flame and Double Red are both natural prominent types forced into midfield by the congested pace map — if either finds a gap to push forward in the first two furlongs, the tactical shape of the race changes materially for every runner behind Alma Latina.

Analogical's Sir Mark Prescott angle is significant — the trainer rarely runs horses without them being primed, and a 12-day return with a course-and-distance profile merits close attention to how quickly Dylan Hogan sends him up to track the leader.

The going is a consistent Good across all Epsom races today with no deterioration noted — no runner has a going concern, but horses proven specifically on Good turf at 1m4f (Analogical, Mr Freedom, Alma Latina) hold the clearest surface edge.

races.name: Betfred 'Follow Us On X' Handicap (Div 1)

runners_data.name: Sarangpur
runners_data.note: Won over 1m4f on Good going most recently and trainer Richard Hughes has a productive 14-day record (2/35 but active); a confirmed hold-up type who fades in the finish suggests he needs a stronger pace than this race may provide, though Good ground and the step back up to today's trip are positive.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap with authority ten days ago, drawing six lengths clear as he tackled 12f for the first time, and further progress seems likely at this trip. He carries a penalty but looked to have plenty in reserve and handles the going well; there should be more to come.

runners_data.name: Dissident
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse who has struggled to compete effectively in recent outings, with zero wins and moderate placings in 15 similar-going runs; the trip looks fine but consistent mid-to-rear finishes and a 21-day break make it hard to find a strong angle.
runners_data.comment: Struggled to see out an extended trip on his most recent start — well beaten after failing to last the distance — and stamina is a clear concern stepping back up here. First-time blinkers are applied, but he has plenty to prove and remains without a win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Thursday
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type who has been running over shorter trips and on Synthetic surfaces in recent starts, posting a string of low finishes; the switch to 1m4f Good turf at Epsom is a big ask and Simon Dow's 14-day record of 0/3 offers little confidence.
runners_data.comment: Thursday trailed throughout at Chepstow last time, unable to get into contention after being held up early, and her form has deteriorated noticeably of late. A first-time hood is fitted but she has a great deal to prove and sits at the foot of our ratings.

runners_data.name: Fram Castle
runners_data.note: Has been off 240 days — the longest absence in the field — and while his form includes a placed effort at 1m5f on Good, his true style is hold-up and he's effectively squeezed into midfield by the volume of similar types; the lengthy break warrants caution.
runners_data.comment: Off the track for 240 days after finishing down the field at Kempton — where he was slow out of the stalls — Fram Castle returns on a lengthy absence and is most effective on the All-Weather over 12-16f. The trainer is in good form but he has much to prove on the comeback and turf is not his ideal surface.

runners_data.name: Dotties Star
runners_data.note: Won over 1m4f on Soft and finished second over 2m on Soft, so stamina is genuine; wears no headgear, holds up naturally, and with 42 days since last run Pat Phelan's team will need him to come on for the break — his real style is at the rear, not the midfield position shown.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Kempton last time out, Dotties Star had shown much better form ahead of that run and this return to turf could see him bounce back into contention. He handles 10-12f and acts on the All-Weather; conditions here may not be ideal but he is not without claims.

runners_data.name: Pablo Prince
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with consistent recent form (4th, 4th in similar company) but zero wins from 15 similar-going runs; his hold-up style means he relies entirely on others to set the pace, and Karen Jewell's yard has not fired in the 14-day window.
runners_data.comment: Finished fourth at Lingfield last time, beaten six lengths on a day when he was below his best at the shorter trip, and this gelding handles 10-12f best on the All-Weather. Yet to score in recent starts, he is an inconsistent sort and hard to rely upon.

runners_data.name: Stintino Sunset
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field and therefore the sole pace-setter; consistent recent record of thirds and a fourth suggests genuine honesty rather than brilliance, and wearing a hood and bit — both adding focus — he should lead throughout under Dylan Hogan on a track that rewards controlled front-running.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and reliable, Stintino Sunset ran to her usual level at Windsor last time out, beaten two lengths off this same mark, and she dons a first-time hood and blinkers today. She handles any going and stays this trip; yet to score in recent starts, her consistency at least ensures she gives herself every chance of filling a place.

runners_data.name: Head Girl
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who posted a placed finish over 1m4f on Good in her most recent run, which is directly relevant form; wears a hood, and David Probert adds a class angle — she's a genuine hold-up type whose best chance comes if the pace is fast enough to stretch the field and leave her a proper gap to thread through.
runners_data.comment: Finished third at Lingfield last time on a mark just 1lb lower than today, beaten two lengths in cheekpieces, and there is scope to build on that here. Effective at 1m4f on fast going, she has solid credentials and rates among the main dangers.

runners_data.name: Panthere Noir
runners_data.note: Showed a placed effort (3rd) over 1m4f on Good at Epsom which is the most course-and-distance relevant form in the field; wears a hood, and while his natural hold-up style is compressed into midfield by the volume of similar runners, apprentice Ryan Kavanagh claiming 5lbs is a notable weight aid.
runners_data.comment: Pulled hard and weakened at Wolverhampton most recently, failing to see out the distance, and he has yet to score in recent starts across a variety of trips. First-time cheekpieces may help him settle better, but he is well below the leaders on our figures and faces an uphill task.

runners_data.name: Lilykoy
runners_data.note: Three-year-old lightly-raced filly stepping up sharply to 1m4f having run all her recent form over 6f-7f; carries the lowest weight in the field and Dylan Cunha's 14-day record of 3/23 is respectable, but the trip extension and inexperience at this distance are significant questions — her natural rear-of-field style is further compressed by the hold-up cluster.
runners_data.comment: Showed more at Windsor last time when beaten 4¼l in a classified race, making a significant step up in trip wearing cheekpieces, and there may be further progress in her. She handles this sort of distance and going; yet to score in recent starts but not without interest.

races.paceDynamic: Stintino Sunset is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 1m4f handicap on Good turf at Epsom, and with no genuine challenger likely to press from the outset, Dylan Hogan can dictate a relaxed, controlled tempo from the front. Epsom's unique undulating track — downhill into the straight — rewards horses that can conserve energy through the middle stages and sprint home, meaning an uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop is a meaningful tactical advantage here. The remainder of the field is almost entirely composed of hold-up horses, several of whom — Head Girl, Fram Castle, Dotties Star, Panthere Noir, Pablo Prince, and Lilykoy — are true rear-of-field types redistributed to midfield on the map simply because the genuine hold-up contingent is too large to represent accurately at the back. This race shape strongly favours Stintino Sunset's front-running profile and any confirmed hold-up horses with the pace to close on a relatively comfortable leader, though true closers face the challenge of generating enough momentum on a track that often blunts late runs when the pace is not strong.

watchPoints.text: Stintino Sunset (Dylan Hogan) — watch whether he is allowed to ping the gate cleanly and secure the rail; if anything forces him to race wider or slower than ideal early, his advantage evaporates immediately.

Panthere Noir — the only runner with a confirmed placed effort specifically at Epsom over 1m4f on Good going; if Kavanagh positions him closer than his redistribution suggests, the course form makes him a live danger to the leader in the straight.

Sarangpur — Richard Hughes is a trainer who places horses precisely and this horse's most recent win was over today's trip on Good; if the pace is strong enough to sustain a late run, he is the most credible closer in the field.

Head Girl — her hood and hold-up style mean she will need a clean passage through the Epsom straight; David Probert is an experienced jockey on tricky tracks and his positioning through the bend will be key to her chance.

Fram Castle — a 240-day absence is the biggest flag in the race; watch the market moves and paddock behaviour, as any significant support would indicate connections believe the layoff has not blunted his ability.

races.name: Betfred 'Follow Us On X' Handicap (Div 2)

runners_data.name: Ricardo Phillips
runners_data.note: A hold-up specialist with strong Good-ground form at 12-14f (1W3P in similar going), this 5yo has been off 240 days but Nicola Currie's record for Henry Candy suggests he arrives fit; his sim-going profile is the most encouraging in this field and he wants a truly-run race to deliver his late finish.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with credit when beaten just over a length off this mark at Kempton, though that run came 240 days ago and the extended absence is the key concern; handles the trip and a sound surface and the mark is not unworkable if he returns close to that level.

runners_data.name: Nymphaea
runners_data.note: Won over 14f on Good ground most recently and ran second over 12f on Soft, so the trip and conditions suit; Marco Ghiani rides and a 6-day turnaround for Jennie Candlish's yard (T14: 4/22) suggests confidence, though her natural hold-up style means she needs the field to spread and create room.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap just six days ago, getting up in the narrowest of finishes in a determined display and now wearing first-time cheekpieces; there is scope for further progress now she has broken her duck and she handles both the distance and this ground.

runners_data.name: Just Adair
runners_data.note: Boasts a superb sim-going record (2W4P from 8 runs on Good), won twice over 12f on this surface, and Billy Loughnane is a strong booking for the O'Neill yard; a tongue-tie is noted and his consistent form figures of 1-1-2-2-8 suggest he fires on this ground — the concern is trip, having not raced beyond 12f.
runners_data.comment: Posted two wins in his last five starts and put in a sound account when beaten just over a length off this mark at Windsor a month ago; the 12f trip on a sound surface suits and the first-time tongue-tie could bring out more, though he will need to convert.

runners_data.name: Gearing's Point
runners_data.note: Redistributed to the lead as the most likely pace-setter despite being a hold-up type in his natural profile (STYLE_FIT 0.80), so his chance depends entirely on whether he consents to make the running; at 8yo his two recent runs (8d, 9d) show active campaigning, but his best form at 12f on Good may not translate to a reluctant front-running role here.
runners_data.comment: Turned her form around sharply to take a classified contest at Brighton by more than two lengths just nine days ago; she wears first-time cheekpieces today and handles the trip and a sound surface, but now carries a penalty and that is the central test.

runners_data.name: Arenas Del Tiempo
runners_data.note: A true hold-up operator pushed into the midfield map slot due to field compression (STYLE_FIT 0.91); his form at 13-16f on Stamina ground is unremarkable (0W1P) and the step down to Good going for Jim & Suzi Best after 121 days off makes this a speculative outing — no win in recent form (6-6736) is a concern.
runners_data.comment: A mare who prefers to set the pace but was left at the start and beaten nine lengths in a handicap at Wolverhampton before this 121-day break; the mark is not punitive but patchy recent form and the layoff combine to make this a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Fighting Poet
runners_data.note: An 8yo who is a genuine hold-up horse shown in midfield due to positional crowding, his bit and recent good-ground form (6/12f/GOO latest) tell a mixed tale; Richard Phillips' yard has 0 wins from 4 in the last 14 days, and a form string of 99-406 makes him difficult to trust in a shape that already disadvantages his natural style.
runners_data.comment: Failed to land a blow in a classified race at Brighton nine days ago and has struggled to make an impact in recent starts; first-time blinkers introduce an unknown element but it is difficult to make a strong case on current figures.

runners_data.name: High Favour
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish, which is a material concern for any horse in a race likely to produce a late sprint; Rose Dawes (5lb claim) rides for the winless-in-14-days Poulton yard, and a form record of 5-0009 across Stamina ground races offers no encouragement — placed into midfield by redistribution, not natural aptitude.
runners_data.comment: Finished well down the field in a handicap at Yarmouth most recently and has been out of contention in the majority of his recent starts; rated lowest in the field, it is difficult to identify a route back to competitiveness.

runners_data.name: Fletcher
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen rides this 3yo for Jim Boyle, who has been quiet (0 wins from 8 in 14 days); Fletcher's best recent effort was 4th over 10f on Good, but he has never won and his step up to 14f is untested — a natural hold-up type shown in midfield only because the map is saturated, his chance depends on the pace being genuinely strong enough to exploit.
runners_data.comment: Beaten around four and a half lengths in a classified event at Windsor most recently and looks a shade more consistent of late after some earlier unplaced efforts; yet to find a way through in recent starts but handles the trip.

runners_data.name: Naranka
runners_data.note: A 3yo lightly raced at sprint-to-mile trips, stepping up sharply in trip to 14f here; Saffie Osborne rides for George Baker (1/10 T14), and a recent 2nd over 12f on Good (his best result) shows some promise, but the unproven stamina and compressed field make it hard to see how he finds daylight in the likely late scramble.
runners_data.comment: Came home strongly at Lingfield most recently, going down by two lengths off a slightly lower mark in a performance that was a clear step forward; he looks capable of competing at this level if he can reproduce that, with 12f a distance he handles.

races.paceDynamic: Gearing's Point is the sole confirmed pace-setter and, despite being a natural hold-up horse redistributed to the front, is the most likely source of early tempo over this 1m4f Epsom trip on Good ground — meaning the pace is likely to be moderate and controlled rather than genuine or pressurised. With the entire field composed of hold-up and midfield types, the race will almost certainly settle into a slow-burn procession through the early stages before a bunched, late-race sprint develops on the descent into the straight. The field holds far more hold-up horses than can realistically settle at the back — Arenas Del Tiempo, Fletcher, Fighting Poet, High Favour, Naranka and others are all true hold-up types mapped forward simply because the race shape forces compression — meaning positional advantage early will be accidental rather than tactical. This race shape strongly favours horses with proven finishing kick over 12-14 furlongs on Good turf who can travel smoothly in mid-division and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out — notably those with demonstrated form over this trip on similar ground.

watchPoints.text: Watch Gearing's Point's early behaviour — if he fails to assert to the front willingly, there may be no genuine pace at all and the race could degenerate into a crawl, making positional luck the dominant factor.
Just Adair's tongue-tie and strong Good-ground record make him the form standout, but his untested stamina beyond 12f at Epsom's undulating 1m4f test is a live concern if the race is truly run.

Ricardo Phillips returns from a 240-day absence and, while Henry Candy runners often arrive ready, the layoff combined with a hold-up style in a race lacking genuine pace could leave him short of the room needed to produce his finishing run.

With six horses legitimately trying to find cover in a nine-runner field, watch the first two furlongs for a positional squeeze — horses drawn wide or ridden aggressively early may gain a crucial tactical advantage in what is otherwise an evenly-matched moderate handicap.

Nymphaea's 6-day turnaround and recent win over 14f on Good are the strongest going/trip credentials in the race — monitor market support as a potential indicator of stable confidence heading into this competitive division.

races.name: Betfred 'Matchday Turbo Boosts' Handicap

runners_data.name: Bella Perla
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here, she has winning form at this trip and on turf but her similar-going record (2 from 9, 0 wins 0 places) on comparable conditions is a mild flag; sole leader in a 10-runner field is a significant tactical advantage and Mitchell knows how to use it.
runners_data.comment: Raced keenly and failed to fire at Yarmouth last time, beaten a long way in a handicap; she is suited by 7/8f and handles All-Weather well, but has significant ground to make up on turf after two poor recent efforts and a step forward is needed.

runners_data.name: Bell Shot
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type with solid placing record at 7f on Good (2 wins 3 places from 15 similar-going runs); headgear (p) in play and 32 days since last run is a normal enough break, but finding a clear passage from the back in a field this cluttered is his chief obstacle.
runners_data.comment: Finished 3¼ lengths adrift at Beverley last time, running short of his recent best off a 1lb higher mark; he tends to make the running and first-time cheekpieces may encourage that, but a big improvement in form is needed from eighth in our rankings.

runners_data.name: Musical Angel
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up filly whose best form includes a win and multiple places over 7f; her similar-going record shows 1 win and 5 places from 11 runs which is solid, though recent form (8th, 5th) is underwhelming and she needs the closers' scenario to materialise authentically.
runners_data.comment: Her course-and-distance form gives genuine cause for confidence — she has landed at Epsom before and is effective at 6/7f on a sound surface; she was well beaten at this course on her latest outing, though the ability she showed on that previous visit means she should not be dismissed.

runners_data.name: Padua
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win over 7f Good in recent memory and a good Crouch-Morrison combination; headgear (t) suggests connections are trying to sharpen him up, and he is well-drawn to slot in just behind Bella Perla — one of the better-placed horses if the front-runner weakens late.
runners_data.comment: Clearly needed his latest Yarmouth outing, managing little after a flat display; prior to that he was in decent form over 7/8f on good ground and All-Weather, the trainer is in form and a first-time tongue-tie is added, giving him a solid chance to bounce back here.

runners_data.name: Utmost Good Faith
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner in the field at OR 87 and a hold-up type by nature; Loughnane and Boughey are a strong combination, and his five recent runs include a 7f win on Standout — his similar-going record (1W 1P from 9) is modest but the class edge is real if the race pans out in his favour.
runners_data.comment: Performed close to his level at Sandown last time, beaten 4 lengths despite a difficult start and tending to race freely; he wears a new combination of hood and tongue-tie and draws wide, though earlier efforts show he is capable — the question is whether his upward curve has peaked.

runners_data.name: Mission Command
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose true style has him mapped to midfield because the rear is too congested; his recent form includes a win (1/7f/SOF) and consecutive third-place finishes, and the trainer's T14 strike rate of 4/22 is respectable — but his style_fit flag means discounting him unless the race completely falls apart.
runners_data.comment: Landed a Chester handicap by 2 lengths last time to end a run without success, showing his best form over a range of trips; a combination of first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces is added as he steps up to a new mark, and he is respected in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Sporting Light
runners_data.note: Progressive three-year-old who won back-to-back over 7f on Standout going; Fahey yard's T14 rate of 5/56 is modest but the horse's own profile suits this prominent position, and 39 days off is a slightly extended break to note — he remains a leading player if he reproduces that winning form.
runners_data.comment: Finished at the back of the field on his first start off a much higher mark, beaten 8 lengths at the same rating he carries here; he sits at the foot of our rankings, draws wide, and another hard afternoon looks likely despite being effective over this trip on any ground.

runners_data.name: Mystic Moment
runners_data.note: Prominent-style three-year-old with places at 7f on Good (1W 4P from 10 similar-going runs) and sits comfortably in the tactical map; 53 days off is the longest absence in the field and Mulholland's T14 of 1/7 does not inspire confidence about race-readiness — fitness is the key question.
runners_data.comment: Kept to her level at Lingfield last time, beaten 8 lengths in a handicap over 7f; she returns from a break and draws wide, and while she is yet to score in recent starts, the ground and trip suit her and our figures rate her competitive here.

runners_data.name: Just Queen High
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature who has been pushed into the midfield mapping due to the overcrowded back end; recent form is patchy (best effort a win on Heathway), and the style_fit discount applies — Bishop is a capable jockey but this horse needs everything to go right from a compromised position.
runners_data.comment: Out of contention throughout at Pontefract most recently, failing to make an impact after being held up; she handles varied going and is effective at 6/7f, but two unplaced finishes from her last three starts make her difficult to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Northern Empire
runners_data.note: Shoemark and Ed Walker is the most potent combination of the redistributed trio, and this three-year-old has a win over 7f on Standout in recent form; by temperament a hold-up horse running out of his preferred position, so the style mismatch must temper expectations, though his natural talent could still surface in a messy race.
runners_data.comment: Ran well adrift at Kempton on his most recent outing, finishing near the back; that was his only start on turf and he has yet to replicate his All-Weather performances on grass — while the connections are well regarded, he needs considerably more to feature here.

races.paceDynamic: Bella Perla is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner handicap and, with no serious pace rival likely to challenge her directly from the front, she should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop over Epsom's 7f on Good ground. Padua, Sporting Light, and Mystic Moment are the prominent types most likely to slot in behind her and keep things honest without turning it into a true test of stamina. The field carries considerably more hold-up intent than the rear of the race can accommodate — Northern Empire, Mission Command, and Just Queen High are genuine closers by nature but have been redistributed to midfield in the map because Bell Shot, Musical Angel, and Utmost Good Faith also want to race from the back, meaning the true hold-up brigade will be squeezed forward against their wishes. With a single uncontested front-runner setting a measured pace and the closers compromised in their ability to get a clear run from deep, this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield horses who can travel within the first five and pounce when Bella Perla comes back to them in the final two furlongs.

watchPoints.text: Bella Perla leads alone and uncontested — if she is allowed to control fractions without any pace rival testing her, she could be very hard to catch; watch whether any of the prominent horses push up early to apply pressure.

The rear of the field is severely congested with Bell Shot, Musical Angel, and Utmost Good Faith all wanting to race from the back — a slow early pace could cause significant traffic issues in the straight for all three.

Padua is wearing a tongue-tie for the first time (hg:t) — first-time headgear can produce a significantly different performance, either sharply better or unsettling; Crouch will need to place him correctly from the front rank.

Northern Empire, Mission Command, and Just Queen High are all true hold-up horses forced into midfield by race shape — if a tight bunch develops turning into the straight, any of them could get a lucky run or, equally, be completely blocked; worth watching the draw and early positioning at the start.

Sporting Light is 39 days absent and Mystic Moment 53 days — the two least race-fit runners in the field are both prominent-style three-year-olds; if either shows any rustiness in the early furlongs, they will be quickly swamped by the front group.
